title: Deployment, Maintenance & Guided Capstone
description: Move a small AI-assisted task application from specification to verified release with monitoring, rollback, and a practical capstone rubric.

lessons.title: From local to deployed
lessons.principle: A deployment publishes a particular artifact to an environment with configuration, network access, and data dependencies.
lessons.practice: List what must differ between local development and production.

lessons.title: Choose a minimal hosting pattern
lessons.principle: A static UI, a server-backed application, and a background worker have different runtime needs.
lessons.practice: Match the hosting approach to actual compute, storage, authentication, and availability requirements.

lessons.title: Configuration and environments
lessons.principle: Development, staging, and production need explicit settings and separation of sensitive state.
lessons.practice: Maintain a sample configuration without embedding working credentials.

lessons.title: Avoid environment drift
lessons.principle: Undocumented production-only changes complicate incident recovery and reproduce failures poorly.
lessons.practice: Version safe configuration, secure secrets separately, and test with staging-like settings.

lessons.title: Build and release gates
lessons.principle: Releases should originate from known source commits and reproducible build steps.
lessons.practice: Run the documented checks and record the tested artifact or commit.

lessons.title: Distinguish checked from unchecked
lessons.principle: A green earlier branch run says nothing definitive about later edits or untested deployment configuration.
lessons.practice: Require the final intended revision to satisfy relevant quality and approval gates.

lessons.title: Continuous integration basics
lessons.principle: CI automates repeatable checks on contributions and helps surface defects early.
lessons.practice: Configure or locate syntax, test, and build jobs appropriate to the project.

lessons.title: Keep CI failures actionable
lessons.principle: A failing check needs its job, command, log, and affected commit identified.
lessons.practice: Fix the underlying cause and rerun against the updated head instead of ignoring a red gate.

lessons.title: Database release planning
lessons.principle: Schema changes may require backward compatibility, migrations, backups, and rollback limits.
lessons.practice: Plan additive changes before removing fields used by deployed clients.

lessons.title: Separate code rollback from data rollback
lessons.principle: Reverting a commit does not reverse every schema or data transformation safely.
lessons.practice: Record migration order, compatibility window, backup point, and recovery procedure.

lessons.title: Monitoring and incidents
lessons.principle: Logs, metrics, alerts, and health signals help operators see what users experience after release.
lessons.practice: Track failed saves, API error rate, latency, and availability without logging private content.

lessons.title: Write a small incident runbook
lessons.principle: During an incident, operators need known symptoms, owners, mitigation, and escalation paths.
lessons.practice: Describe how to detect failed task creation, disable the feature, restore service, and communicate status.

lessons.title: Capstone scope: task tracker
lessons.principle: An end-to-end task tracker is a bounded project that exercises UI, validation, storage, testing, and release.
lessons.practice: Commit to create, list, complete, and reload tasks as the initial deliverable.

lessons.title: Make AI optional to product runtime
lessons.principle: Using AI to develop the application does not require sending users' tasks to a third-party model.
lessons.practice: Use AI for planning, code explanation, cases, and review while keeping the core tracker functional offline if chosen.

lessons.title: Capstone build in slices
lessons.principle: A vertical slice makes one real journey work before adding optional features.
lessons.practice: Build task creation end to end, then listing, completion, persistence, and failure messages.

lessons.title: Write a checkpoint for each slice
lessons.principle: A slice is complete only when its requirement, code, and observable test agree.
lessons.practice: Commit independently verifiable changes and retain a short checklist of what remains.

lessons.title: Capstone acceptance and review
lessons.principle: Demonstrated behavior is stronger evidence than a generated code listing or polished mockup.
lessons.practice: Test blank-title rejection, stable IDs, create/reload/complete, error feedback, and keyboard interaction.

lessons.title: Conduct an AI-assisted final review
lessons.principle: The model should inspect the actual diff and look for risks and missing cases, not merely praise its own output.
lessons.practice: Assign a human to inspect findings and validate fixes on the intended final revision.

lessons.title: Operations and continued learning
lessons.principle: Shipping begins maintenance; feedback and telemetry inform future iterations without overriding product scope.
lessons.practice: Record known issues, supported platforms, setup, and recovery notes.

lessons.title: Choose a next learning path deliberately
lessons.principle: A finished beginner project can branch into frontend, backend, SQL, Git, Docker, or advanced AI workflows.
lessons.practice: Select the next Facts topic based on the weakest tested competency and the needs of your next project.

codeExamples.snippet:
Release checklist
[ ] Final requirements and scope reviewed
[ ] Automated checks run on final SHA
[ ] Manual UI/keyboard flow checked
[ ] Secrets and permissions reviewed
[ ] Recovery or rollback documented

Capstone demonstration
1. Create a task with valid input.
2. Reject an all-whitespace title.
3. Reload and preserve a stable task ID.
4. Complete the same task.
5. Simulate save failure and show honest feedback.
6. Review the diff and document residual risk.
